subject.title: RFC: TapesClaw for Claw telemetry storage and querying

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a first-party, default-bundled durable telemetry store and the proposed `skill_workshop.evidence` extension boundary?
rationale: This is a new product capability that affects user data collection, install-time consent, persistent storage, and a future plugin API; implementation quality cannot determine those policies.

options.title: Sponsor a privacy-first RFC
options.body: Accept the direction in principle, then require the RFC to specify consent, retention, redaction, access controls, failure behavior, and a stable hook contract before implementation.

options.title: Keep telemetry external
options.body: Decline default bundling and direct the work toward an optional external integration unless a future core extension gap is demonstrated.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Leave the RFC unaccepted until a maintainer can set the telemetry and Skill Workshop product boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a privacy-first RFC
recommendation.body: Accept the direction in principle, then require the RFC to specify consent, retention, redaction, access controls, failure behavior, and a stable hook contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available PR discussion identifies them as the only named participant in the underlying product conversations; this is a low-confidence routing signal, not an ownership claim.
